title: Valid Parenthesization With Wildcards
statement: Read a string made only of the characters '(', ')' and '*', where each '*' may be treated as either '(', ')', or the empty string. Print 'true' if there is some way to interpret every '*' so that the whole string becomes a validly balanced parenthesization, otherwise print 'false'.
starter_code:
s = input().strip()

# TODO: determine whether `s` can be validly parenthesized when each '*'
# is freely treated as '(', ')' or empty. Track the range [lo, hi] of
# possible open-paren counts as you scan left to right: '(' increases
# both bounds, ')' decreases both, '*' decreases lo and increases hi.
# Clamp lo at 0 (can't go negative), and bail out to "false" early if hi
# ever goes negative. At the end it's valid iff lo can be exactly 0.
# Print "true" or "false".
hints: Track the minimum and maximum possible count of unmatched open parens as [lo, hi] while scanning left to right
'(' does lo+=1, hi+=1; ')' does lo-=1, hi-=1; '*' does lo-=1, hi+=1
Clamp lo to 0 after each step (never let it go negative), and stop early with false if hi < 0
